title: attn-harmony: fused attention kernel with rope/rotary coordinator and shadow-KV scheduler
author: Liam Chen
commits: feat: introduce harmony fused attention kernel (prototype)
perf: optimize tiling and fp16 accumulation path
feat(kv): add shadow KV scheduler with warmup hints
test: add long-sequence and streaming integration tests
ci: add bazel target and perf CI job
description: Context and motivation: Operating teams continue to hit a tradeoff between low tail latency and unit cost when serving long-context transformer workloads. Existing FlashAttention variants we onboarded earlier reduce compute but require multiple fallbacks across rotary/rope variants and separate KV eviction policies. This PR introduces 'attn-harmony', a single fused attention kernel plus a lightweight coordinator that unifies rope/rotary offsets, fuses softmax+reduction for reduced memory hops, and integrates with a new shadow-KV scheduler to prewarm likely-to-be-used KV shards. Goals: reduce p50/p95 latency, improve throughput under continuous batching, and simplify runtime fallbacks so routing can favor a single optimized path for most models. Design highlights: 1) Harmony kernel implements a fused qk->softmax->attn*V path with an optional fused rotary application step; the kernel exposes a fastpath when rotary embeddings are contiguous or stride-1, and a generic path for legacy layouts. 2) Coordinator: small CPU-side shim that canonicalizes rotary/rope offsets across model variants, rewrites per-request metadata to align KV indexing, and calculates per-request tiling hints for the batcher. 3) Shadow-KV scheduler: runs alongside the real KV cache and simulates warmups using low-priority prefetch requests driven by the coordinator's access predictions; scheduler supports soft eviction scores and sequence-aware aging. 4) Continuous batching: the batcher consumes coordinator tiling hints to create tighter-preserving batches (minimizing padding) and to decide when to opportunistically fuse short sequences into micro-batches to keep GPU pipelines full. Implementation notes: - Harmony kernel written in CUDA with templated FP16/FP32 paths and explicit FP16 accumulation where beneficial. - Uses per-warp tile transposes to avoid global transpose passes for many common layouts. - Rotary normalization step implemented inline with minimal kernel divergence; when stride-1 rotary is detected the kernel takes a specialized vectorized path. - Coordinator is intentionally lightweight (single-threaded control loop per worker) to avoid adding scheduling jitter. - Shadow-KV scheduler operates with capped bandwidth and backpressure so it cannot starve user requests. Benchmarks (on p4d-like instance, sequence lengths 512/2048/8192, batch sizes tuned per test): - 512: p50 latency -10% vs baseline, p99 -6%, throughput +8% - 2048: p50 -18%, p99 -12%, throughput +22% - 8192 (long context): p50 -25%, p99 -18%, throughput +30% - Under continuous batching microbench (mixed seq distribution), cost per token reduced ~14% while maintaining target p95 SLO. Compatibility and fallbacks: - Kernel registers itself under existing kernel registry and advertises capabilities; the runtime will prefer harmony when model flags for rotary/rope are set or when coordinator canonicalization can be applied. - For models with bespoke rotary layouts, runtime falls back to the generic harmony path or the legacy kernel. Testing and CI: - Added unit coverage for rotary normalization and tiled transpose. - Integration tests exercise streaming, long-context KV prewarm, and canary can run with scripts/canary_rollout_attn.sh. - Perf CI job added that runs longseq_microbench.py and uploads trace artifacts. Rollout plan: 1) Canary in staging fleet for 48h using low percentage traffic with shadow-KV enabled. 2) Monitor p50/p95 and cost per token metrics; rollback if p99 regresses >5% or error rates increase. 3) Gradually increase to 25% then 100% if stable. Risk and mitigations: - Numerical regressions: added golden-model evals against reference kernels; nightly regression alerts in Optimize linked to prompt sets. - Scheduler bandwidth could induce pressure; we cap shadow prefetch and include dynamic backoff. - Edge-case rotary layouts: coordinator logs and auto-falls back to legacy kernel with telemetry to prioritize additional layout support. Checklist: - [x] Kernel correctness tests - [x] Integration tests for streaming and KV warmup - [x] Perf benchmarks run and reviewed - [x] Docs updated (ops/harmony_kernel.md) - [x] Canary rollout script included Related Linear tickets: ENG-3218 (kernel work), ENG-3302 (kv scheduler), ENG-3375 (perf CI).
review_comments: Aisha Patel: Please add a p99 breakdown by GPU utilization and kernel occupancy for the 2048/8192 runs; also ensure the FP16 accumulation path has stochastic rounding disabled by default.
Liam Chen: Added perf artifacts under perf/trace and verified FP16 path uses deterministic rounding; updated CI to capture occupancy metrics.
Marcus Li: Concerned about coordinator adding scheduling jitter; can we confirm single-threaded loop introduces <200us variance at 1000 RPS?
Liam Chen: Measured end-to-end variance with synthetic load; coordinator adds ~80us median and ~170us 95th at 1000 RPS on our staging VMs, added numbers to benchmark notes.
Sofia Ramirez: Shadow-KV scheduler could be noisy; request a circuit-breaker if prefetch error rate increases or if total cache spill grows beyond threshold.
Liam Chen: Implemented breaker that disables shadow prefetch for 5m if any of the safety heuristics trip; added telemetry counters.
Evan Brooks: Approve after seeing the long-seq integration tests and canary rollout plan.
release_notes: Introduce attn-harmony: a fused attention kernel with integrated rotary/rope coordinator and a shadow-KV scheduler that reduces latency and improves throughput on long-context workloads. Opt-in via runtime kernel flags; canary rollout required. Provides ~15-30% throughput improvements and 10-25% p50 reductions across tested sequence lengths.
